intro: Excerpts copied from the live M2V source (C:\M2V). M2V is an early-stage project, so this set is proportionate — it covers the real pipeline (lyric direction, audio segmentation, image+video generation, FFmpeg assembly), the API/job model, and the standalone proof-of-concept that actually rendered a video. Everything runs locally; there are no external AI keys.

snippets.title: One process, both faces — API thread + UI
snippets.explanation: The default `python main.py` runs the FastAPI API in a daemon thread and the Gradio UI in the main thread, so one command brings up both the :8501 API and the :7841 console. The logs confirm this path works — m2v.log shows the API and UI starting and answering /health on 2026-06-09 and -10.

snippets.title: QI module contract endpoints
snippets.feature: Standard health/identity any QI project can call
snippets.explanation: The three QI contract endpoints (/health, /version, /info) let the QI Hive dashboard and sibling projects discover M2V and check it is alive. These are the parts of M2V verified live — tests/test_smoke.py asserts exactly this shape. (Note: /info still advertises legacy backend names that the live engine no longer uses.)

snippets.title: Submit a job, run it in the background
snippets.explanation: Generation is long (~20-30 min), so the endpoint returns a job_id immediately and runs the pipeline on a background daemon thread. As run_pipeline() yields progress events they are appended to the job's event list, which the UI polls via /api/status/{id}/events. JOBS is an in-memory dict — simple, but it means a restart loses all job history (a database is on the roadmap).

snippets.title: The five-stage generator
snippets.code:
yield {"stage": "analyzing", "message": "Analyzing lyrics with LLM\u2026"}
audio_duration = get_duration(audio_path)
scenes: list[Scene] = analyze_lyrics(lyrics, audio_duration, style=style)
yield {"stage": "analyzed", "n_scenes": len(scenes),
       "scenes": [asdict(s) for s in scenes]}

# align audio timestamps onto the scenes
timestamps = get_section_timestamps(audio_path, len(scenes))
for i, (start, end) in enumerate(timestamps):
    scenes[i].start_time = start; scenes[i].end_time = end

generator = VideoGenerator(reference_image_path=reference_image_path, ip_scale=ip_scale)
for i, scene in enumerate(scenes):
    duration = max(scene.end_time - scene.start_time, 3.2)
    clip_path = os.path.join(scenes_dir, f"clip_{i:03d}.mp4")
    yield {"stage": "generating", "clip_index": i, "total_clips": len(scenes), ...}
    generator.generate(prompt=scene.prompt, negative_prompt=scene.negative_prompt,
                       duration=duration, output_path=clip_path)
    clip_paths.append(clip_path)
generator.unload()
snippets.explanation: The whole product is this one generator function. It writes a scene prompt per lyric section, segments the audio to give each scene a time window, generates one clip per scene, then assembles. Being a generator means it can `yield` a status dict after every step — which is exactly what the API turns into the UI's live progress log, with no extra streaming machinery.

snippets.title: Local LLM as music-video director
snippets.code:
system_prompt = (
    "You are a music video director. For each song segment, create a vivid visual scene "
    "description optimized for AI image generation. Be specific about lighting, setting, "
    "subject, and atmosphere. Avoid abstract concepts \u2014 describe concrete visual scenes.")

resp = requests.post(OLLAMA_URL, json={
    "model": OLLAMA_MODEL,            # qwen3:8b
    "prompt": user_prompt, "system": system_prompt,
    "stream": False, "think": False,
    "options": {"temperature": 0.7}}, timeout=120)
raw = resp.json().get("response", "")
match = re.search(r'\[.*\]', raw, re.DOTALL)   # pull the JSON array out
if match:
    return json.loads(match.group())
snippets.explanation: Rather than naively turning lyrics into prompts, M2V asks a local Ollama model (qwen3:8b) to act as a director and return a JSON array of {prompt, mood, color_palette} — one per song section. `think:false` suppresses the reasoning-model preamble; a regex pulls the JSON array out of whatever the model wraps around it. Runs entirely on the local Ollama server, so it costs nothing and stays private.

snippets.title: Structure-aware lyric splitting with fallbacks
snippets.explanation: Lyrics arrive in every shape, so the splitter degrades gracefully: first it honours explicit [Verse]/[Chorus] markers, then falls back to blank-line paragraphs, then to fixed 4-line chunks. _auto_label() even guesses chorus vs verse by spotting repeated paragraphs. The result is capped to 10 scenes (adjacent shortest segments merged) to keep render time sane.

snippets.title: Fallback prompt when Ollama is down
snippets.feature: Pipeline never dies just because the LLM is offline
snippets.explanation: If the Ollama call raises or times out, the analyzer logs it and builds a simple prompt straight from the first two lyric lines plus the chosen style modifier. It is cruder than the LLM's output but keeps the pipeline producing scenes — a recurring 'produce something rather than crash' theme across M2V.

snippets.title: Structural segmentation with even-split fallback
snippets.feature: Place scene boundaries on the song
snippets.code:
y, sr = librosa.load(audio_path, sr=22050, mono=True)
mfcc = librosa.feature.mfcc(y=y, sr=sr, n_mfcc=13)
bounds = librosa.segment.agglomerative(mfcc, k=n_segments + 1)
bound_times = librosa.frames_to_time(bounds, sr=sr)
times = sorted(set([0.0] + list(bound_times) + [duration]))
while len(times) - 1 > n_segments:        # merge the shortest gap
    gaps = [(times[i+1] - times[i], i) for i in range(len(times) - 1)]
    gaps.sort()
    times.pop(gaps[0][1] + 1)
return [(round(times[i],2), round(times[i+1],2)) for i in range(len(times)-1)]
snippets.explanation: To make cuts land near real musical sections, the analyzer computes MFCCs and runs librosa's agglomerative clustering to find structural boundaries, then trims to exactly the number of scenes by merging the shortest gaps. If librosa is missing or fails, get_section_timestamps() silently falls back to an even time split — the video still gets sensible scene windows.

snippets.title: Lyrics from tags first, Whisper second
snippets.code:
lyrics = _from_id3(audio_path)          # USLT/SYLT embedded tags
if lyrics:
    print(f"[lyrics_extractor] Found embedded lyrics ({len(lyrics)} chars)")
    return lyrics

print("[lyrics_extractor] No embedded lyrics \u2014 transcribing with Whisper\u2026")
lyrics = _from_whisper(audio_path, whisper_model)
if lyrics:
    return lyrics
raise LyricsNotFound("No embedded lyrics and Whisper transcription returned empty.")
snippets.explanation: Reading lyrics from embedded ID3 tags is instant and exact, so it is tried first; only when a song has no embedded lyrics does M2V fall back to transcribing the audio with Whisper (which is slower and approximate). If both come up empty it raises LyricsNotFound rather than guessing.

snippets.title: SDXL still, optionally IP-Adapter-conditioned
snippets.code:
self._sdxl = StableDiffusionXLPipeline.from_pretrained(
    SDXL_MODEL, torch_dtype=dtype,
    variant="fp16" if device == "cuda" else None, use_safetensors=True).to(device)
self._sdxl.enable_attention_slicing()

if self._ref is not None:
    self._sdxl.load_ip_adapter(IP_ADAPTER_REPO, subfolder="sdxl_models",
                               weight_name=IP_ADAPTER_WEIGHT)
    self._sdxl.set_ip_adapter_scale(self._ip_scale)
...
kwargs = dict(prompt=prompt, negative_prompt=negative_prompt,
              num_inference_steps=30, guidance_scale=7.5, width=1024, height=576)
if self._ref is not None:
    kwargs["ip_adapter_image"] = self._ref
return self._sdxl(**kwargs).images[0]
snippets.explanation: Each scene's still comes from SDXL Base 1.0. If the user supplied a reference photo, IP-Adapter is loaded and the photo is passed as ip_adapter_image so the same face/style carries across every scene — the project's answer to AI videos where the cast changes every shot. The scale slider (ip_scale) tunes how strongly the photo constrains the output.

snippets.title: Animate the still with Stable Video Diffusion
snippets.feature: Turn each image into real motion
snippets.code:
frames = self._svd(image, num_frames=SVD_FRAMES,        # 25 frames
        num_inference_steps=25, decode_chunk_size=8,
        motion_bucket_id=127, noise_aug_strength=0.02,
        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)).frames[0]

tmp = output_path.replace(".mp4", "_raw.mp4")
export_to_video(frames, tmp, fps=SVD_FPS)               # 8 fps -> ~3.1s

clip_dur = SVD_FRAMES / SVD_FPS
loops = max(1, round(duration / clip_dur))
cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-stream_loop", str(loops - 1), "-i", tmp,
       "-t", str(duration), "-vf", f"scale={OUT_W}:{OUT_H}",
       "-c:v", "libx264", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-preset", "fast", output_path]
snippets.explanation: SVD produces a fixed 25-frame (~3.1s) clip from the still. Because a scene usually needs to be longer, FFmpeg loops the raw clip enough times to fill the scene's duration and scales it to the 1280x720 output. The fixed seed keeps motion deterministic. (The loop-to-fill approach can look repetitive on long scenes — non-looping motion is a roadmap item.)

snippets.title: Two 8GB models sharing 16GB of VRAM
snippets.feature: Alternate load/unload to fit the GPU
snippets.code:
def generate(self, prompt, negative_prompt, duration, output_path):
    img_path = output_path.replace(".mp4", "_frame.png")
    image = self._make_image(prompt, negative_prompt)   # loads SDXL
    image.save(img_path)
    self._unload_sdxl()        # free ~8GB before SVD loads
    self._animate(image, max(duration, 3.2), output_path)   # loads SVD
    return output_path
snippets.explanation: SDXL (~8GB) and SVD (~8GB) won't both fit comfortably in the RTX 5080's 16GB, so generate() makes the image, explicitly unloads SDXL and empties the CUDA cache, then loads SVD to animate. This per-scene swap is the main reason a 10-scene video takes ~20-30 minutes, but it keeps peak VRAM within budget.

snippets.title: Mux the original song over the cut
snippets.feature: Final video carries the real audio track
snippets.explanation: After the SVD clips are concatenated, the silent video is muxed with the original song: the video stream is copied as-is, the audio is re-encoded to AAC 192k, and -shortest trims to whichever track ends first. This is what makes the output an actual music video synced to the song rather than a silent montage.

snippets.title: Burn lyrics in as timed subtitles
snippets.code:
with open(srt_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for i, scene in enumerate(scenes, 1):
        start = _srt_time(scene.start_time); end = _srt_time(scene.end_time)
        lines = [l.strip() for l in scene.lyrics.splitlines() if l.strip()][:2]
        f.write(f"{i}\n{start} --> {end}\n{chr(10).join(lines)}\n\n")
...
cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", video_path,
    "-vf", (f"subtitles='{srt_escaped}':force_style='FontName=Arial,FontSize=22,"
            "PrimaryColour=&HFFFFFF,OutlineColour=&H000000,Bold=1,Outline=2,"
            "Shadow=1,Alignment=2,MarginV=20'"),
    "-c:a", "copy", out]
snippets.explanation: An SRT is written straight from the scene start/end times (first two lyric lines per block) and burned into the video with FFmpeg's subtitles filter and an explicit caption style. Real .srt files with timed Portuguese captions exist in data/output, confirming this path runs. Subtitles are optional via the UI's 'Burn subtitles' toggle.

snippets.title: Ken Burns scene, or a labelled placeholder
snippets.feature: make_forro_video.py — render even with missing frames
snippets.code:
try:
    if not os.path.exists(img_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(img_path)
    base = ImageClip(img_path)
    cover = max(w / base.w, h / base.h)              # scale to fill frame
    clip = (base.with_duration(duration)
                .resized(lambda t: cover * (1 + ZOOM * t / duration))  # Ken Burns
                .with_position("center"))
    return clip
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning(f"Scene {scene['n']:>2} MISSING '{scene['image']}' ({e}); using placeholder")
    bg = ColorClip(size=resolution, color=PLACEHOLDER_BG).with_duration(duration)
    ...  # overlay a [label] caption and continue
    return bg
snippets.explanation: This is the standalone track that actually rendered M2V's first full video (forro_anime_mv.mp4, 160s). Each scene gets a slow Ken Burns zoom; if a scene image is missing it logs a warning and substitutes a labelled placeholder rather than aborting — which is exactly what happened on the proof-of-concept run (all 10 frames were placeholders, per forro_video_build.log) so the render still completed.

snippets.explanation: An alternative image source for the standalone track: a stdlib-only urllib client builds a canonical SDXL text-to-image graph in ComfyUI's API format and POSTs it to a running ComfyUI, then polls /history for the result. It uses core nodes only so it loads on any ComfyUI install. This is wired but not yet run — which is why the proof-of-concept video still uses placeholder frames.
